summary: Ephemeral worker retry-loop and inflight queue saturation causing elevated 5xx for customer tenant
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 01:40 UTC ClearLedger observed a sharp rise in 5xx responses (primarily 502/503) from the Redwood API. Errors correlated with sustained client concurrency from their dedicated tenant. Impact: ClearLedger experiences failed generation calls and truncated streaming responses; several customers reported degraded UX. Environment: Dedicated capacity in us-east serving gptx-13b-v1 (pinned). Symptoms: - API gateway returning 502/503 intermittently for requests routed to tenant pool. - Upstream runtime logs show repeated worker process restarts (~OOM or forced exit) followed by rapid reconnects. - Autoscaler reported frequent scale events for ephemeral pool and then rate-limited backoff. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run ClearLedger's traffic replay (provided) with ~350 concurrent streaming sessions pinned to gptx-13b-v1. 2) Observe increased tail latencies and then 502/503 error rate rising past 8% within 15 minutes. 3) Check runtime worker processes on affected nodes for restarts. Logs & metrics: - apigw: elevated 5xx rate beginning 2026-03-10T01:40Z; spike correlated to tenant burst (ingress qps +180%). - runtime: repeated worker PID churn, exit code 137 and watchdog restarts. - autoscaler: oscillation of ephemeral worker group between 2 -> 8 nodes then rapid drain. Immediate customer-facing impact: Calls failing, streaming sessions dropping, higher token costs due to retries. Workaround requested: Temporarily rate-limit the tenant to 200 concurrent sessions or change model pin to a smaller instance type. Follow-ups: SRE to validate root cause and recommend durable mitigation (autoscaler tuning, backoff safeguards, and worker watchdog parameters).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Retry loop combined with prefetch/backpressure caused inflight queue saturation on scheduler layer, leading to kernel-level memory pressure and worker OOMs. Evidence: - Worker exit codes 137 in /var/log/runtime/worker.log. - dmesg entries indicate process killed by OOM killer on worker nodes that experienced high KV cache miss rates. - Autoscaler logs show reactive scaleouts followed by rapid drains (node reuse delay ~30s) leading to connection thrash. Secondary hypothesis: a recent runtime patch to do aggressive prefetching (PR 4221) increased resident set for certain prompt shapes, pushing close to GPU memory limits under high concurrency. Actions taken so far: - Scoped impacted tenant and applied a temporary ingress concurrency cap at the API layer (200). - Disabled prefetch for the tenant via routing override (will revert after fix validated). - Collected core dumps and GPU memory snapshots and uploaded to S3 (links in comments). - Eng on-call reproduced a smaller-scale replay and confirmed worker churn starts around 250 concurrent sessions. Next steps: - Runtime team to revert aggressive prefetch patch for the dedicated pool and run canary (priority). - Autoscaler to add minimal cooldown and stabilize drain behavior to avoid oscillation. - SRE to investigate if libcudart or driver versions on these nodes are correlated with higher-than-normal fragmentation. - Coordinate with ClearLedger to schedule a controlled traffic ramp test once mitigations are in place.
